chapters.title: Read moves and learn a stage

prompts.text: One turn. A new possibility. Learn it here. Try it in your hands.
Start with one small step. You do not need to know how to solve yet.
Find your starting point. Or join a lesson if you already know where to begin.
Choose your current level. Pick what you can do on your own today.
Choose a way of thinking. Layers and pairs, or blocks and the middle slice?
Be honest about your foundation. Roux routes are included when they fit your experience.
Choose a goal. Here, we want a first independent solve.
Choose your practice habits. Short sessions count. At the club, at home, or both.
Read the reason for your route. This example starts with LBL. Open the first lesson when ready.
Match the starting hold. Here: white on top, green in front.
U / D: up / down. L / R: left / right. F / B: front / back.
Plain letter: clockwise 90°. A prime mark reverses it. A 2 means a half turn.
Choose U′, then Direction view. Look straight at the upper face to judge its direction.
Play the move. Watch the top layer, then copy it on your cube.
Replay, or return to Holding view. Changing the camera changes your view, not the cube.
Build a white daisy. Put white petals around the yellow centre first.
Use the example setup. Open “Follow along with a physical cube”.
Apply its scramble from solved. Start white-up, green-front. Pause the video to prepare.
Return to the player. Read Observe, Prepare and Check the result.
Try Next move. Copy one turn, then check what changed.
Follow whole-cube rotations too. A shown x, y or z is a real regrip. Camera dragging is only a view change.
Start with a method you know. Choose LBL while learning your first independent solve.
Paste the scramble you used. Only use this option if that sequence was applied from solved.
Choose Explain with LBL. The site checks and builds your teaching steps.
Follow the solution player. Match the holding, then use Next move.
Keep the physical cube in sync. A stage jump changes the display; it does not turn your cube.
Choose Enter colors. Follow the holding diagram for the current face.
Pick a colour, then a sticker. Centres are fixed. Copy your actual cube.
Continue through all six faces. Keep the top and front directions shown for each face.
Review and Check colors. Finish every face and correct errors before solving.
Try to name the case. Study the diagram before you reveal the answer.
Show the solution. Check the holding and formula. Repeat when it feels familiar.
Scramble from solved. Start white-up, green-front and apply the printed moves.
Check the six-face diagram. Compare its stickers with your cube.
Hold Space until Ready. Release to start the timer.
Press again to stop. On a touch screen: hold, release, then tap to stop.
Inspection is optional. Use the checkbox when you want inspection before timing.
Review your times and averages. ao5 and ao12 summarize five and twelve solves.
Correct a result when needed. Use +2 for a penalty or DNF for an unfinished solve.
Export a backup. Keep CSV or JSON before clearing data or changing devices.
Roux builds two side blocks. It uses the middle slice instead of treating every layer separately.
Read the setup and block check. Different pieces can suggest a square, a pair, or another construction.
Try one explained example. Follow the shown hold. M and M′ turn the middle slice.
Progress at your own pace. The lessons and CMLL library explain the next stages.
Lab explores candidate routes. It can compare white or yellow bottoms and different left colours.
Read the recommendation carefully. Move counts and handling scores are references, not promises of speed.
Follow the selected route. Use the player, then compare it with another on a physical cube.
Keep notes about the feel. Trials help compare the same starting cube. Your records stay local.
Open Guide and pick a chapter. Find the instructions for the page you are using.
Expand Every control, explained. Look up a button without replaying the whole video.
Try a page tour if you need it. Choose one thing to practise today, then try it with your cube.
Your turn. Keep your curiosity. Learn it here. Try it in your hands. Full guide: open Guide.
